body.heading: The clues
paragraphs: A lock has a three-digit code. You do not know whether digits repeat — the clues will settle everything. Here they are. 682: one digit is correct and in the right place. 614: one digit is correct but in the wrong place. 206: two digits are correct but both in the wrong places. 738: nothing is correct. 780: one digit is correct but in the wrong place.
Resist the urge to guess. This puzzle is fully solvable by elimination, and the most powerful clue is the one that tells you nothing is there.

body.heading: Solving it step by step
paragraphs: Start with 738: the digits 7, 3 and 8 appear nowhere in the code. Now look at 780 — its one correct digit cannot be 7 or 8, so it is 0, and since it is in the wrong place, 0 is not the third digit. In 206, two of 2, 0, 6 are correct but misplaced; 0 sits in the middle there and is misplaced, so 0 is not the second digit either. A digit that is neither second nor third must be first: the code starts with 0.

Next, 682 has exactly one correct digit in the right place, and 8 is already eliminated. If 6 were correct in first place, that would clash with our 0 — so the correct one is 2, sitting third. Now 206 has its two correct digits accounted for: 2 and 0, both misplaced, which means 6 is not in the code at all. Finally 614 needs one correct digit in the wrong place; 6 is out, and the digit that fits is 4, which cannot sit third (that place belongs to 2), so it goes in the middle.

body.heading: The code, and how to make your own
paragraphs: The code is 042. Run it back through all five clues and each one checks out exactly — that final verification is part of the puzzle, not an optional extra.

To build your own, pick a code, then write clues that are each true of it, mixing 'right place', 'wrong place' and 'nothing' types. Test it on a friend: if they reach a single answer by reasoning alone, your clue set is complete.

takeaway: The code is 042 — and notice how the 'nothing is correct' clue did the heavy lifting first. Elimination is a superpower.
